title: Growth-brain and persona-review cron results are never delivered ('unknown platform webui')
evidence: cron/jobs.json: tc-growth-harness-brain (43b0d5c4446d, hourly) and tc-weekly-persona-review (8d3ac21799d5, Mon 09:00) both report last_status=delivery_failed. The overnight watchdog logged the same thing twice: "result not delivered — unknown platform 'webui'". Every hourly growth report and the weekly persona review are therefore written to disk and thrown away.

notes.note: OUT OF REPO SCOPE - recorded, not acted on. This is Hermes cron config (~/.hermes/profiles/turbo-carnival/cron/jobs.json), not the turbo-carnival repo. Likely fix: `hermes cron edit <id> --deliver <target>` with a platform the gateway actually serves. Needs Tim to say which destination he wants the growth reports on; the ops-triage job's own delivery works, so the gateway has a working target elsewhere.

Refreshed 2026-09-19 14:4x EDT. The blast radius grew: tc-ops-triage itself now reports last_status=delivery_failed with last_delivery_error unknown platform webui, so this fix loop own reports are among those thrown away (growth-brain 14:02 and weekly-persona-review are unchanged failures). Root cause pinned mechanically: deliver=origin with origin.platform=webui, and gateway/config.py Platform has no webui member and no bundled plugin platform of that name, so _prepare_target_delivery returns None before any send. Run output is still written to cron/output/<job-id>/*.md, which is why continuity and the next tick can still read it. This profile has NO messaging platform configured at all (no platforms: block in config.yaml; channel_directory.json lists homeassistant and email with empty lists), so the only valid targets are local and bot-chat. local would flip last_status to ok while still delivering nothing to Tim - that hides the failure rather than fixing it, so it is rejected. bot-chat is the designed destination for a webui-originated job, but it injects the report as a message the bot answers: a full agent turn per delivery, hourly for the growth brain, which is a spend change needing Tim explicit ok. Blocked on Tim naming a destination; the fix is one command per job, e.g. hermes cron edit 43b0d5c4446d --deliver bot-chat.

Ops-triage 2026-09-19 20:2x UTC: unchanged, blocked on Tim naming a delivery destination. Confirmed again this run -- this job's own report is in the same boat (last_status=delivery_failed, unknown platform webui). Run output still lands in cron/output/<job-id>/*.md, so continuity is intact; local would only mask the failure and bot-chat changes spend. No action taken (Hermes config, outside this repo).

2026-09-19 21:3x UTC ops-triage re-verified. Still broken and now confirmed mechanically: gateway/config.py Platform has 25 members (LOCAL, TELEGRAM, DISCORD, ... EMAIL, HOMEASSISTANT, ...) and NO webui member, so deliver=origin with origin.platform=webui can never resolve -- the report is written to cron/output/<job-id>/*.md and then dropped. jobs.json: tc-growth-harness-brain (hourly) and tc-weekly-persona-review (Mon 09:00) both last_status=delivery_failed, and tc-ops-triage (this fix loop) is in the same state -- verified last_status=delivery_failed, last_delivery_error unknown platform webui, last run 17:05. So this loop own reports are discarded too; the board under ops/board/ is the only durable record of what it found. The ONE job that reports ok is tc-overnight-watchdog, which uses deliver=local -- that flips the status to ok while still delivering nothing to Tim, so it hides the failure rather than fixing it and is rejected as a fix. channel_directory.json lists homeassistant and email with EMPTY channel lists and config.yaml has no platforms block, so this profile currently has no messaging destination at all. BLOCKED ON TIM: name a destination (add an email/telegram channel, or accept bot-chat knowing each delivery injects the report as a message the bot answers = an extra agent turn per hour). Fix is one command per job once named, e.g. hermes cron edit 43b0d5c4446d --deliver <target>, plus a gateway restart to pick up jobs.json.
